blocks.text: Church, David had just come back from the valley with the giant's head in his hand. King Saul called him in and asked him whose son he was. And while David was talking to the king, somebody else was listening.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jonathan was the king's son. He was next in line for the throne. By the world's way of counting, David was his competition. But Jonathan did not count like the world counts.

verses.text: Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.

blocks.text: Say it with me. Somebody say, he held nothing back. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "He held nothing back"] He held nothing back. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "He held nothing back"] His robe, his sword, his bow, his belt. Jonathan gave it all.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: That is covenant friendship. Not the kind that is there when things are good and gone when things get hard. The kind that says, what is mine is yours.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: And things did get hard. Saul turned on David and wanted him dead. When Jonathan spoke up for his friend, his own daddy threw a spear at him. So the two of them made a plan. David would hide out in the field, and Jonathan would come out to shoot arrows. Where the arrows fell would tell David whether it was safe to come home.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Look at that. Two grown men, a warrior and a prince, holding on to each other in an empty field, crying. David cried the hardest. There is no shame in a man's tears, Church. Not when love is real and goodbye is hard.

verses.text: And Jonathan said to David, Go in peace, forasmuch as we have sworn both of us in the name of the LORD, saying, The LORD be between me and thee, and between my seed and thy seed for ever. And he arose and departed: and Jonathan went into the city.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: They went their separate ways that day. But they had put their friendship in the LORD's hands, and the LORD kept it. Years later, when David was king, he went looking for Jonathan's son, to show him kindness for his father's sake. Some friends are a gift straight from heaven. Thank God for the ones who stick closer than a brother.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to 1 Sam 18:1-4 and 20:35-42; the spear is 20:33, the kindness to Jonathan's son 2 Sam 9; covenant friendship only, nothing read into it.

cultural.note: Warm preaching cadence; men's tears honoured without a joke; 'his own daddy' once, natural; call and response 'he held nothing back' tied to the gifts, not last.
